string.name: guide_pad_intro
string.value: Play the console's games with a controller or keyboard on this device.

string.name: guide_pad_enable_title
string.value: Turn it on on the console first

string.name: guide_pad_enable_body
string.value: The console has to allow it: in SFT on the console, turn on "Controls from the viewer" on the Beta page (SFT 0.7.20 or later). Then open the menu at the top center while streaming and tap Controller; it says it is connected.

string.name: guide_pad_connect_body
string.value: Pair the controller by Bluetooth in the system settings, or plug it in by USB. "Pressing" on the Controller page of the menu shows the buttons and sticks live, so you can check every button first.

string.name: guide_pad_one_body
string.value: SFT gives each client one controller on the console. Every controller on this device, and the keyboard, are merged into that one. For two players, the second one uses the console's own controller.

string.name: guide_pad_layout_body
string.value: By default buttons go by position: the bottom one is B and the right one is A, as on the console's own controller. Choose "By label" in Settings if you prefer the letters. Start is +, Select is −, the middle button is HOME, and the shoulder buttons and triggers are L / R / ZL / ZR.

string.name: guide_pad_keyboard_body
string.value: No controller? Use a keyboard: WASD is the left stick, IJKL the right stick, the arrow keys the D-pad; Z X C V are A B X Y; Q / E are ZL / L, O / U are ZR / R; F / H click the left / right stick; = is +, - is −, Home is HOME. The first key you press connects it to the console.

string.name: guide_pad_menu_body
string.value: While the menu is open, the controller does not play the console. With only a controller in hand, hold Start and Select (+ and −) for 1.5 seconds to open the menu. When the app goes to the background or the stream ends, this controller is unplugged from the console.

string.name: guide_pad_trouble_title
string.value: Sticks not moving, or wrong buttons

string.name: guide_pad_trouble_body
string.value: Sticks and analog triggers need HarmonyOS 5.0.3 or later; on older systems only the buttons work. If the character keeps moving after you let go, raise "Stick dead zone" in Settings. This feature is still in testing; if a controller's buttons come out wrong, please tell us its model.

string.name: vpad_haptic_desc
string.value: A light buzz when you press an on-screen button

string.name: vpad_autohide_desc
string.value: Hide the on-screen buttons while a real controller is connected

string.name: guide_pad_touch_body
string.value: This is experimental and still being tuned; see the known issues below. No controller? While streaming, open the menu at the top center, go to Controller and turn on "Touch controller" to get on-screen buttons (needs a touchscreen). Touch anywhere on the empty left half for the left stick; where you touch is its center. You can slide between the face buttons, the D-pad directions and the shoulder buttons. While they are shown, tapping the picture does nothing; after a few seconds the menu button shrinks to a short line at the top center, and tapping it opens the menu. "Arrange buttons" on the Controller page lets you move, resize or hide buttons, or turn on L3 / R3; tap Save to keep it. Tablets, unfolded foldables and other wide screens can also play upright; see "Layouts and portrait".

string.name: guide_pad_touch_issues_body
string.value:
1. A shaky network makes it hard to use: when streaming over the network, the buttons travel on the same connection as the picture, so when the picture stutters, presses arrive late or get lost and the stick can jump around. If the network drops for more than 3 seconds, the console lets go of the controller and takes it back when the stream returns. The dedicated hotspot or a network cable on the console helps a lot; USB is not affected.
2. Some games ignore it: on the console it is one more controller, and games that only listen to player 1 won't react. Move it to the first place in Controllers > Change Grip/Order on the console's HOME menu.
3. It has not been tested enough in real games yet; the feel and latency will keep improving. Feedback is welcome.

string.name: vpad_edit_desc
string.value: Drag each button to move it; resize, hide, or turn on L3 / R3

string.name: vpad_edit_hint
string.value: Landscape layout: drag to move, tap to select

string.name: vpad_edit_hint_selected
string.value: Use − / + to resize. Faded buttons are hidden; select one to show it

string.name: vpad_wide_only
string.value: Only in a wide-screen state (tablet, wide foldable, unfolded foldable and the like)

string.name: vpad_layouts_desc
string.value: View, create, change and delete your own layouts

string.name: vpad_layout_builtin_desc
string.value: Built in, follows the screen size; cannot be changed

string.name: vpad_layout_custom_active_desc
string.value: Your own layout; tap Edit to change it

string.name: vpad_layout_name_taken
string.value: A layout with that name already exists

string.name: vpad_layout_delete_message
string.value: Delete "%s"? If it is in use, the default layout takes its place.

string.name: vpad_layout_saveas_title
string.value: The default layout cannot be changed. Save as a new layout

string.name: vpad_layouts_note
string.value: Landscape and portrait each keep their own layouts and remember which one is in use, so landscape can put the buttons over the picture and portrait can keep them below it. Layouts are saved as proportions of the screen, so they work on other screen sizes; editing turns the screen to that placement.

string.name: guide_pad_layouts_body
string.value: Settings → Touch controller → Manage layouts: landscape and portrait each have a default layout (around the edges in landscape, below the picture in portrait) you can base your own on, then edit, rename or delete; each remembers which one it uses, so landscape can put the buttons over the picture and portrait can keep the picture on top and the buttons below. While streaming you can change layouts on the Controller page of the menu and tap Arrange to change one. On tablets, unfolded foldables, wide foldables and other wide screens you can stream in landscape or portrait: pick "Screen orientation while streaming" (Follow system, Landscape, Portrait) in Settings or under Streaming options in the menu. Phones and the outer screen of foldables stay landscape.

string.name: guide_pic_pos_body
string.value: When there is empty space above and below the picture (a tablet held upright, an unfolded foldable, a tri-fold and so on), tap "Picture position" in the menu while streaming and drag the picture up or down; it snaps to the top, center and bottom. Tap Save to keep it. Each screen shape (folded, unfolded, rotated) remembers its own position. The picture and the touch controller are separate layers: moving the picture never moves the buttons. In portrait the picture starts at the top and the buttons at the bottom; if the picture now covers some buttons, drag them clear with "Arrange buttons".

string.name: vpad_edit_hint_portrait
string.value: Portrait layout: drag to move, tap to select
